scope_note: Corrective public-evidence and model-eligibility audit for Markley Group's Lowell data center at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County. The selected IM3 footprint is one building inside a three-building assessor parcel, so every sourced amount remains at campus or company/county scope and is unallocated to the selected building. State and City records preserve Phase I forecasts, cumulative investment, operating-headcount, TIF-savings and incentive evidence; assessor and tax records provide parcel-value stocks and one complete billed-tax year; permits provide discrete administrative values and contractors; MEPA and MassDEP records establish supporting electric work and permit-listed generators; and two recipient records verify separate community contributions. Forecasts, cumulative values, parcel stocks, billed taxes, permit values, permit-authorized equipment, white-space area and recipient funding remain distinct and non-additive. Source-family gap closure found no audited annual construction outlay, construction workforce or payroll, vendor payments or local-purchase share, facility payroll, metered annual electricity, project-attributable utility-upgrade cost, annual water or wastewater series, actual emissions, cash tax receipts, marginal public-service cost, fiscal net or causal county outcome. One last-resort synthesis survives: the exact FY2026 real-property-bill amount is reused only as a same-account public-service-cost break-even threshold, not as observed cost, collected revenue or a net fiscal result; all other contribution and GDP, employment and wage candidates are rejected individually in the project updates.

project_updates.title: Boundary and chronology audit — selected building kept separate from the campus
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: IM3 inventory geometry and provenance; Markley current and archived operator pages; Lowell assessor parcel P90290/MBLU 184/4765/2; 2015, 2018, 2020, 2023 and 2024 City planning and bond records; deed/sale fields; and web archives. The evidence supports a June 2015 purchase, Phase One open with customer occupancy by November 23, 2015, a three-building 14.4-acre assessor parcel, a later 65,000-square-foot expansion approval and continuing equipment changes. It does not map the selected 123,665-square-foot inventory footprint to an assessor building number or allocate campus investment, jobs, capacity, incentives or current white space to that polygon.
project_updates.project_description: Markley Group's Lowell data center operates at 2 Prince Avenue/1 Markley Way in Lowell, Middlesex County, Massachusetts, on the former Prince Pasta factory site. The selected IM3 footprint represents one building within a three-building assessor parcel, so campus-wide investment, employment, value, capacity, and incentive facts remain unallocated to that building. Markley reported Phase One open with customers occupying space by November 23, 2015 and now describes the Lowell facility as 352,000 square feet of secured white space. City planning records separately document a 2018 approval for a 65,000-square-foot expansion and later cooling, water-tank, generator, and utility modifications.

project_updates.title: Investment, incentive and fiscal audit — forecasts separated from cumulative observations
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: the 2015 EACC approval release; City TIF summaries and FY2020-FY2026 budgets; the 2023 preliminary official statement; EDIP awardee, annual-report, compliance and decertification pages; City Council agendas, minutes and attachments; assessor history; Treasurer/Collector billing; municipal audits/ACFRs, capital plans and check-register/vendor searches; and official-statement debt disclosures for 2015-2026. Queries used Markley, Markley Group LLC, Markley Boston LLC, 2 Prince Avenue, 1 Markley Way, P90290, 184/4765/2, 2015-2035 TIF and EDIP. FY2020 records execution in May 2015, and the 2017 summary identifies a clawback and Middlesex 3 membership; the signed agreement, payment schedule and annual compliance ledger were not located. The fragment retains the $72.8 million Phase I plan, $104,121,860 cumulative-investment observation, $77,182,505 combined local incentive forecast, $187,500 approved state credit, $1,624,655.79 cumulative real-estate TIF savings and a separate $534,231.97 FY2026 real-property bill. Adopted-budget documents 20496, 23767, 26555 and proposed-budget document 30950 have no Markley row. InvoiceCloud returned all four FY2026 real-property quarters with zero balances, but billed tax is not cash received and the portal does not identify payment versus adjustment; partial FY2025/FY2027 displays are excluded, and the personal-property query returned no open invoice, which cannot establish historical liability or exemption value. Fiscal candidate decisions: an annual-receipt or net-fiscal model is rejected because recipient distributions, cash collections, realized personal-property relief and same-scope public costs are missing; a statutory TIF counterfactual is rejected because the executed schedule and annual baseline are absent. The sole eligible public-cost candidate reuses the exact FY2026 bill only as the same-account $534,231.97 service-cost break-even identity. It is decision-relevant and reproducible but is neither observed cost nor a surplus/deficit and must not be summed with the bill.

project_updates.title: Assessor and parcel audit — four annual real-property stocks added

project_updates.title: Resource, utility and environmental audit — permit equipment added; consumption remains unallocated
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: MassDEP air-plan applications, notices and OADR decisions under 24-AQ02F-0001-APP/NE-25-002, including the March 27, 2026 final decision and July 2026 reconsideration docket; Lowell Planning Board, Sustainability Council, water, sewer and data-center materials; fuel-storage licensing; National Grid and Massachusetts DPU dockets and tariffs; ISO New England queue and reliability material; EPA facility searches; Markley facility, PPA and sustainability pages; and 2025-2026 reporting based on water bills or operator statements. The City authorized four 6,000-gallon diesel tanks in July 2025; a later fuel-license amendment application filed September 8 was withdrawn October 13, so no additional capacity is inferred. Licensed tank capacity is not fuel inventory or use and the vocabulary has no matching storage-capacity metric. AP reports an operator-stated summer peak of about 118,000 gallons per day, but no meter ledger or annual total was published and the vocabulary has no direct actual peak-water metric. A Markley solar PPA covers a broader company purchase in Eversource territory and is not allocated to the National Grid-served Lowell site. No facility annual electricity, demand, tariff payment, grid-upgrade cost, verified annual water/wastewater, generator runtime, fuel use, actual emissions or selected-building resource series was found.

project_updates.title: Community-recipient audit — one recipient-verified Lowell contribution added
project_updates.notes: Source families checked: University of Massachusetts Lowell, Middlesex Community College, Greater Lowell Community Foundation, Merrimack Valley Food Bank, Lowell Public Schools, youth sports, libraries, housing and other food-assistance recipients; City packets; Markley press and social pages; and local news archives for grants, sponsorships, donations, STEM, education and volunteer support from 2015-2026. Queries combined Markley or Markley Group with each recipient and contribution term. UMass Lowell lists Markley Group in the $25,000 Signature Sponsor tier for the May 1-2, 2026 Meehan Student Center dedication. The event's more-than-$300,000 total is not attributed to Markley. A separate recipient page verifies a $25,000 2025 Merrimack Valley Food Bank gift; no complete annual Middlesex County grant register, in-kind valuation, volunteer-hour series or campus-attributable total was found. Community-model candidate: annualizing, averaging or extrapolating the two gifts is rejected because they are distinct episodic transfers, the recipient universe is incomplete and neither is allocated to the campus or selected building.

project_updates.title: County-outcome eligibility audit — GDP, employment and wages rejected separately
project_updates.notes: The repository county economic panels for 2001-2024, study-county exclusions, inventory history and the direct evidence above were reviewed with a November 2015 opening anchor and 2007-2014 candidate pre-period. Markley is not Middlesex County's first known data-center operation: the governed first-entry evidence documents earlier colocation in Somerville, while Markley's 2018-2026 expansions prevent a single stable post-treatment boundary. GDP candidate: difference-in-differences, event-study and synthetic-control designs are rejected because exposure predates the anchor, treatment intensity changes and no defensible unexposed donor design or project allocation is available; a descriptive benchmark gap is also rejected as insufficiently decision-relevant because it cannot distinguish Markley from Middlesex County's large, diverse economy. Employment candidate: the same identification failures apply, and the 26, 31 and 101 facility snapshots neither measure county employment change nor define annual-average FTE. Wage candidate: the same identification failures apply, no project payroll or occupation mix was found, and nominal county average weekly wages would mix industry composition and inflation. Each outcome therefore remains an explicit gap; no descriptive comparison is presented as causal. No records requests or other solicitations were made.

project_updates.title: Corrective investment and construction model screen — direct records remain non-additive
project_updates.notes: Gap-closure searches covered Lowell Planning Board applications, drawing sets, stormwater reports, staff memoranda, minutes and conditions for 2015, 2018, 2020, 2023 and 2024; Inspectional Services monthly issued-permit files for January 2024-June 2026; CSS online permitting and City outage guidance; permit IDs BLD202400574, ELC202406426, BLD202413857, ELC202507553 and BLD202603584; contractors Willard L. Cleveland, New England Electric Group, Coordinated Systems Consulting, Saiful Bouquet and Stantec; and operator, trade and archive searches under both addresses and parcel P90290. The 2024 memorandum confirms proposed equipment and utility work but supplies no expenditure or completion amount. Investment candidate: annualizing the $104,121,860 cumulative FY2020-labeled observation or allocating it to the selected building is rejected because its expenditure dates, asset mix and building allocation are unknown. Construction candidate: summing permit valuations or applying construction multipliers is rejected because the amounts are administrative estimates with unresolved building/trade overlap, no audited spend, no equipment exclusion, no duration, no worker/payroll input and no local-purchase share. The approximately $200 million campus forecast and $72.8 million Phase I plan remain forecasts and cannot replace those missing inputs.

project_updates.title: Corrective supplier and operations model screen — eligibility is not evidence of payment
project_updates.notes: Supplier and procurement searches covered COMMBUYS and ITS86 under Markley Boston LLC and master blanket PO-26-1080-OSD03-OSD03-39704; City vendor/check-register, capital-budget and council-payment searches under Markley, the named construction firms and the two site addresses; contractor portfolios; operator customer/career pages; Massachusetts workforce, apprenticeship and wage-enforcement sources; and archived job listings for 2015-2026. ITS86 confirms only contract eligibility and a 3 percent supplier-diversity commitment, not a purchase order, invoice, Lowell performance location or payment. Supplier candidate: applying a transferred local-purchase share or indirect multiplier is rejected because no vendor payment base, geography, timing or non-overlap evidence exists. Household-spending candidate is rejected because construction and operating payroll are absent. Operations candidate: interpolating 2019, 2020 and 2025 headcount snapshots or multiplying them by county/occupation wages is rejected because the stocks are not annual-average FTE, roles and compensation are unknown, the Lowell-resident count is only a nested subset, contractors/customers are not measured and no selected-building allocation exists.

project_updates.title: Corrective utility, environmental, infrastructure and legal-financing screen
project_updates.notes: Searches covered MEPA archive and Environmental Monitor entry EEA 15988; Massachusetts EEA facility/permit search; MassDEP application 24-AQ02F-0001-APP, approval NE-25-002 and OADR 2025-022 decisions; EPA facility indexes; Lowell water, wastewater, stormwater, fuel-license and Sustainability Council files; National Grid/Massachusetts Electric dockets, tariffs and project materials; Massachusetts DPU and ISO New England indexes; operator PPA/sustainability pages; registry/deed references Book 29147/Page 49; City budgets, ACFRs, official statements, bond/TIF/PILOT/IRB and legal-agreement files; and public financing searches for Markley Group LLC, Markley Boston LLC, 1 Markley Way and 2 Prince Avenue over 2015-2026. EEA 15988 directly ties a fully constructed 23-kV line project to Markley's load but gives no cost, customer contribution, subsidy, demand or selected-building allocation and says no Commonwealth financial assistance was sought. Resource candidate: converting the 50-MW approval-stage plan into annual electricity or the reported 118,000-gallon summer peak into annual water is rejected because neither is metered annual use, operating capacity is unverified, load/cooling factors are absent and all figures are campus-wide. Infrastructure-cost and financing candidates are rejected because EEA 15988, the air docket, the deed, City debt files and searched TIF materials disclose no compatible project cost, payment, borrower balance or allocation. Permit limits and equipment counts are not emissions, fuel use or public cost.

project_updates.title: Recipient-side gap closure — second separate contribution retained
project_updates.notes: The Merrimack Valley Food Bank site was searched by Markley and Markley Group for 2015-2026 and opened the recipient-hosted November 2025 report. It verifies a $25,000 emergency-food-drive donation supporting Lowell families. The record is retained separately from the 2026 UMass Lowell $25,000 sponsorship because the recipients, purposes and years differ. Operator/campaign claims of a $40,000 youth-baseball contribution and a combined $30,000 for two other events were not added because recipient-side ledgers or an exact recipient split were not found in the reviewed public results. The two retained gifts do not define a recurring series, annual campus total, in-kind value or selected-building contribution.

project_updates.title: GDP source review — county series cannot identify the project
project_updates.notes: BEA annual county real-GDP files and the repository's 2001-2024 governed panel were reviewed for FIPS 25017, with a candidate 2007-2014 pre-period, 2015 opening anchor and exclusion of all study counties from possible donors. The series is available, but the causal and descriptive candidates are rejected for the project-specific reasons recorded in the county-outcome eligibility audit: earlier Middlesex data-center activity, changing Markley exposure after 2015, concurrent county shocks, no selected-building allocation and inadequate decision relevance for an unattributed descriptive gap.

project_updates.title: Employment and wage source review — county context stays non-causal
project_updates.notes: BLS QCEW county employment and nominal average-weekly-wage files and the repository's 2001-2024 governed panel were reviewed for FIPS 25017, with the same candidate 2007-2014 pre-period, 2015 opening anchor and study-county donor exclusion. Employment and wage comparisons are each rejected: the county series do not measure Markley FTE, payroll, occupations or compensation; prior data-center exposure and later campus phases defeat a stable treatment; and nominal wage changes mix inflation and county industry composition. No county gap is labeled or published as a facility effect.
